channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Tajikistan to expand electricity supplies to Afghanistan's Badakhshan province
item.description: Pamir Energy and Afghanistan's Da Afghanistan Breshna Sherkat (DABS) have amended an electricity supply agreement. Supplies will continue to border areas of Badakhshan province, serving 6,900 consumers. The agreement also includes expanding electricity exports via Pamir Energy's networks and constructing new power lines.

item.title: Kazakhstan may require social media to faster remove insults and illegal photos
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Internal Affairs is considering requiring social media platforms to expedite the removal of illegally used images and insults. This follows a proposal to enhance protections for citizens whose images are broadcast or used in live streams without consent. The ministry will review complaint procedures.

item.title: Kazakhstan aims to host major international chess tournaments, President Tokayev states
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with FIDE President Timur Khayrulin to discuss developing Kazakhstan's chess school. Tokayev congratulated Khayrulin on his election, highlighting Kazakhstan's growing international prestige in chess. He emphasized chess's role in intellectual development and outlined priorities for strengthening national teams and youth talent.

item.title: Kazakhstan intends to host major international chess tournaments, state media reports
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated Kazakhstan's intention to host major international chess competitions during a meeting with FIDE President Timur Turlov, according to Akorda's press service. Tokayev highlighted chess's importance for intellectual development and noted the success of the women's team at the World Chess Olympiad. Priorities include strengthening teams and developing infrastructure.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Meets New FIDE President Timur Turnov
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev congratulated Timur Turnov on his election as the new head of the International Chess Federation (FIDE). Tokayev emphasized the growing authority of Kazakhstan and its chess school globally. He highlighted chess as a tool for developing youth intellectual potential and noted the progress of the Kazakh chess school, with over 278,000 active participants.

item.title: Kazakh President Assigns Important Tasks to Timur Turnov
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with Timur Turnov, the newly elected President of the International Chess Federation (FIDE). Tokayev congratulated Turnov, stating his election reflects Kazakhstan's growing global authority in chess. He highlighted chess's importance for youth intellectual development and noted over 278,000 people actively participate in the sport in Kazakhstan.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Discusses Chess Development with FIDE President Turlov
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with FIDE President Timur Turlov to discuss the development of chess in Kazakhstan. Tokayev congratulated Turlov on his election, highlighting Kazakhstan's growing international authority in chess. He emphasized chess's role in intellectual development and noted the sport's progress in the country, with over 278,000 active players and recent successes by the women's team.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Epidemiological Situation Regarding Plague Remains Stable, Says Health Committee
item.description: Uzbekistan's epidemiological situation concerning the plague is stable, with 53 sanitary control points operating at borders to prevent the import and spread of dangerous infectious diseases. The Sanitary-Epidemiological Committee stated this in response to inquiries. Reports of suspected plague cases in Irkutsk, Russia, are being monitored, but the situation in Uzbekistan is not a cause for concern.

item.title: Talan Towers to Cover Costs for Cars Damaged by Hurricane in Astana
item.description: Talan Towers in Astana will cover all expenses for car owners whose vehicles were damaged when a piece of facade detached due to hurricane-force winds and fell onto parked cars. The administration acknowledged responsibility, stating the incident is an insurance case. Any remaining costs not covered by insurance will be compensated by Talan Towers from its own funds.

item.title: Almaty plans to redevelop former industrial zones into residential areas
item.description: Almaty's new master plan until 2040 aims to relocate 276 industrial enterprises outside the city. Former industrial zones will be cleared for new housing, offering potentially more attractive locations than outskirts. Experts warn buyers to investigate soil remediation due to potential contamination from former factories.

item.title: Kazakhstan explores larger Trans-Caspian oil export route amid CPC disruptions
item.description: Kazakhstan's major oil producers are studying a larger Trans-Caspian export route as an alternative to the Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC), which has faced repeated disruptions. A feasibility study for transporting crude via the Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan pipeline is underway, aiming to diversify export options beyond the CPC's dominant role.

item.title: Tashkent State Technical University: Nearly 300 students evicted from dormitory
item.description: Approximately 300 students were evicted from a dormitory at Tashkent State Technical University built on a public-private partnership basis. Students claim they paid fees in advance but were expelled due to the building lacking a license and alleged "orders from above."

item.title: Kazakh MP proposes biometrics for money transfers over 50,000 tenge to combat crime
item.description: A Kazakh Member of Parliament has proposed implementing biometric verification for money transfers exceeding 50,000 tenge. The measure aims to protect youth from involvement in drug crimes and 'droppering' (acting as money mules), citing statistics on drug-related offenses and youth involvement.

item.title: Kazakhstan-New York direct flight launch postponed to second half of 2027
item.description: The launch of direct flights from Kazakhstan to New York has been postponed to the second half of 2027. Previously planned for early 2027, the delay is due to ongoing technical audits, obtaining necessary permits, and awaiting the arrival of new aircraft.

item.title: Uzbek President Sends Greetings to International Forum on Food Security
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev sent greetings to participants of an international forum dedicated to food security. The message was read by the president's press secretary. The forum also coincided with International Cotton Day and addressed food security for landlocked developing countries.

item.title: Two Individuals Arrested in Astana for Transporting Large Quantity of Drugs
item.description: Police in Astana have arrested a 20-year-old man and an 18-year-old woman for attempting to transport a significant amount of drugs into the capital. During a search, officers found two vacuum-sealed packages containing approximately 2 kilograms of mephedrone. A further kilogram was discovered at their rented apartment.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes Reserve Work Mode for Doctors During Internet Outages
item.description: A proposal has been made in Kazakhstan to implement a unified reserve work procedure for medical organizations to address technical failures or internet disruptions. The initiative aims to ensure uninterrupted medical care, especially in remote areas, by creating a single patient anamnesis within medical information systems, including chronic conditions and allergies. Alternative patient identification methods are also suggested.

item.title: Kazakhstan Diversifies Economy Beyond Raw Materials, Boosting GDP and Investment
item.description: Kazakhstan is actively diversifying its economy beyond its traditional raw material sector, aiming to reduce reliance on volatile global commodity prices. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev prioritizes developing manufacturing and infrastructure. This strategy has led to significant growth, with GDP per capita exceeding $15,000 and attracting $114.2 billion in foreign direct investment between 2021-2025.

item.title: Kazakhstan Farmers Request Delay of Baqylauda Monitoring System Until 2028
item.description: Kazakhstan's agricultural producers are requesting a postponement of the Baqylauda monitoring system's implementation until 2028. A deputy proposed the delay, arguing that the system currently imposes an excessive administrative burden. The proposal also calls for revising requirements regarding employee numbers and labor costs, considering agricultural automation and the need for sustainable development.

item.title: Uzbekistan Establishes Real-Time Security Situational Center for Students
item.description: Uzbekistan is enhancing student safety by establishing a digital technology-based situational center in the 'Yoshlik' student campus. This center monitors the campus in real-time, tracks attendance, and prevents offenses. The initiative is part of a broader national effort to create a secure environment for youth, with 33 billion soums invested in the center and campus improvements.

item.title: Russian Army Deserter Expelled from Kazakhstan After Illegal Border Crossing
item.description: A former Russian army soldier, who deserted in July 2025 and illegally crossed into Kazakhstan in March, has been ordered expelled from the country. He was apprehended by the National Security Committee while attempting to reach Taraz. The court waived a large fine due to amnesty but upheld the expulsion and a five-year entry ban.

item.title: US Major Convicted of Killing 13 to Face Death Penalty
item.description: US President Donald Trump has approved the execution of former Army Major Nidal Malik Hasan, who killed 13 service members in 2009. USA TODAY reported that Hasan will be executed by lethal injection, a decision Trump approved based on the recommendation of the Secretary of Defense. The last military execution occurred in 1961.

item.title: Yemen's Houthi Rebels Attack Airports in Riyadh and Aden
item.description: Iran-backed Houthi rebels claimed responsibility for ballistic missile attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and Aden International Airport. The attacks reportedly disrupted air traffic and caused flights to be diverted. The Saudi-led coalition stated it intercepted a missile targeting Riyadh. These incidents occurred amid ongoing conflict in Yemen.

item.title: Prosecutor Seeks Lengthy Prison Sentences for Sultanbekov and Atambayev in Bishkek Trial
item.description: In a Bishkek court, prosecutors are demanding significant prison terms for social democrats accused of "violent seizure of power" and "mass riots." The prosecution is seeking 9.6 years for Sultanbekov and 7.6 years for Atambayev, as the trial continues into alleged involvement in these serious offenses.

item.title: Kazakhstan Deputy Proposes Minimum Payment Protection for Bank Accounts
item.description: A deputy from the "Aul" party has proposed introducing a protected minimum payment when restricting citizens' bank accounts. Citing data on problem loans and frozen accounts, the deputy argued that individuals need access to funds for essential living expenses like transport, utilities, food, and medicine.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Establish Unified Ministry of Education and Science
item.description: Uzbekistan announced the reorganization of its education system, merging the Ministry of Preschool and School Education with the Ministry of Higher Education, Science, and Innovation into a single Ministry of Education and Science. The reform aims to create a unified system from preschool to higher education and improve quality.

item.title: Turkmen President and Russian President hold phone conversation
item.description: Turkmen President Serdar Berdimuhamedow and Russian President Vladimir Putin held a phone conversation. Berdimuhamedow congratulated Putin on his birthday and expressed gratitude for his attention to Turkmen-Russian relations. Putin acknowledged the strong ties based on equality and mutual respect.

item.title: Kazakhstan develops test system to detect meat product falsification
item.description: Kazakh scientists have developed a PCR test system to identify the species composition of meat and detect raw material substitution in meat products. The Ministry of Agriculture stated the system can identify DNA from 17 animal and bird species, simultaneously detecting multiple species in one sample.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon congratulates Vladimir Putin on birthday
item.description: On October 7, 2026, Tajik President Emomali Rahmon spoke with Russian President Vladimir Putin by phone. Rahmon congratulated Putin on his birthday, wishing him health and success. The leaders expressed confidence that Tajik-Russian relations will continue to develop for the benefit of both nations.

item.title: Russian Forces Launch Large-Scale Missile and Drone Attack on Ukraine, Two Killed in Kyiv
item.description: Russian forces conducted a massive strike on Ukraine using ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, and drones on October 7, 2026. Two people died in Kyiv, with damage reported in several districts. Attacks also targeted Dnipro, Zaporizhzhia, Kremenchuk, and Pryluky, hitting industrial and transport infrastructure.

item.title: Atyrau Refinery Disputes Environmental Inspection Findings on Emission Calculations
item.description: The Atyrau Refinery disputes the findings of an unscheduled environmental inspection regarding emission calculations for certain technological furnaces. The refinery states it possesses the necessary calculations performed within its current environmental permit, refuting claims of non-compliance reported by the Ministry of Ecology and Natural Resources.

item.title: Explosion in Faizabad Injures Two Civilians, Taliban Official Targeted
item.description: An explosion occurred in Faizabad, the provincial capital of Badakhshan, on Wednesday, October 7. The Taliban confirmed two civilians were injured. Sources indicated the explosion targeted a vehicle carrying the Taliban's chief judge in Badakhshan, reportedly caused by a mine.

item.title: Tajik Opposition Urges Release of Journalist Rukhshona Khakimova at OSCE Conference
item.description: At a conference in Warsaw, representatives of Tajik opposition groups called for the release of journalist Rukhshona Khakimova, sentenced to eight years for her research on China's influence. The opposition argues her harsh sentence is solely due to her work, which they believe is not anti-state but a pursuit of reform and human rights protection.

item.title: CIS and SCO Counter-Terrorism Forum Convenes in Minsk
item.description: The fourth CIS and SCO Counter-Terrorism Forum has begun in Minsk, focusing on combating terrorism and extremism. Participants will exchange national experiences and discuss international cooperation, including joint measures against transnational crime and online extremist content. The forum also includes exercises like 'Eurasia-Antiterror—2026'.

item.title: Taliban Court Chief's Vehicle Targeted in Mine Blast in Badakhshan, Afghanistan
item.description: Local sources in Badakhshan province report that a mine explosion targeted the vehicle of the Taliban's chief judge. The incident occurred in Faizabad. Details regarding injuries and the condition of the judge remain unclear, amidst recent attacks on Taliban officials in the region.

item.title: Tashkent Mayor: City needs approximately $2 billion annually for development
item.description: Tashkent Mayor Shavkat Umurzakov stated that the city requires about $2 billion annually for development, including infrastructure, social services, and revenue-generating projects. He specified allocations for roads, communal infrastructure, and social sectors like schools and healthcare, emphasizing the need to maintain an investment environment.

item.title: Tashkent to host international mining and metallurgy dialogue
item.description: Tashkent will host the 20th International exhibition "Mining, Metallurgy and Metalworking – MiningMetals Uzbekistan 2026" from October 27-29. The key event will be the 8th Uzbekistan International Mining and Metallurgy Forum (UIMF 2026), focusing on "From Resources to Global Opportunities." Discussions will cover expanding Central Asia's resource base and critical mineral extraction.

item.title: Kyrgyz Citizens Injured in Mass Brawl Involving Foreigners in South Korea
item.description: A mass brawl involving foreigners occurred in Pyeongtaek, South Korea, on October 3rd. Reports suggest around 40 individuals, possibly from Central Asian countries, were involved. Two Kyrgyz citizens and two Russian citizens were detained. Three Kyrgyz citizens were reportedly injured, with one requiring surgery.

item.title: Tajikistan and Iran Abolish Visas for Citizens, Effective October 5, 2026
item.description: Tajikistan and Iran have fully implemented a visa exemption for holders of ordinary passports, effective October 5, 2026. Citizens can stay in the other country for up to 30 days within a 90-day period without a visa, provided they comply with national laws. This applies to international border crossings.

item.title: UN chief urges voluntary, safe return of Afghans from Pakistan
item.description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres called for the voluntary, safe, and dignified return of Afghans from Pakistan, where millions have been deported since a repatriation campaign began in 2023. The UN will continue working with Pakistan to protect Afghans affected by the campaign, ensuring returns are voluntary and dignified.
